title: The effect of flipped learning on academic performance as an innovative method for overcoming ebbinghaus’ forgetting curve
reason: Per-student LMS video view counts (dichotomised: fewer vs more than two views) compared on final exam scores by independent-samples t-test in a flipped mathematics-education class. Meets I1; small sample, dichotomised indicator.

extraction.design: single-class flipped-learning study; indicator-group t-test; pre/post self-efficacy
extraction.n_quote: Participants consisted of sophomore students (n=37, 26 male, 11
extraction.population: sophomore students in Introduction to Mathematics Education, 1 university
extraction.lms_indicators: LMS view counts of the lecture movie clip (attendance rate of LMS data)

effect_sizes.between: LMS video view count ('Less than 2 times' vs 'More than 2 times') ↔ final exam score

extraction.notes: Table 1 group rows: 'Less than 2 times' N 23, M 54.22, SD 23.36; 'More than 2 times' N 14, M 72.71, SD 24.23 (column order N, Mean, SD from header). Grouping cut-off wording ('less than 2' vs 'more than 2') leaves exactly-2 unclear. Self-efficacy pre/post is a separate group-level analysis.
